news.title: Morocco U15 Finish 13th at World Cup in Azerbaijan With 36 Goals
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s U15 national football team finished 13th in the 2026 U15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, ending their campaign with an impressive attacking record of 36 goals. The tournament brought together 189 countries, with Morocco securing eight victories in ten matches despite suffering elimination in the round of 16 against Paraguay. The Atlas Cubs began their campaign with five consecutive victories in the group stage, demonstrating their attacking strength from the opening match. Morocco defeated the Philippines 2-0 before securing a 4-2 victory over Costa Rica.

news.title: Breaking: Spain win inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup
news.lede: October 30, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports 0. Spain have been crowned champions of the inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival after defeating the Czech Republic 3-0 in Friday’s final in Baku, Azerbaijan. The Spanish youngsters delivered a commanding performance at the Baku Crystal Hall to claim the first title in the newly introduced competition, which brought together young footballers from across FIFA member associations. Goals from Tiago Polo, Bruno Fernández and Adrián Bielsa secured the historic victory for Spain, who completed their campaign with an impressive record under coach David Gordo.

news.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
news.lede: Infantino said in 2023 equality was Fifa’s target. Prize money could double but big gap will remain. Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament. Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambition was to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.”

news.title: England Under-15s in fresh World Cup controversy after uncontested penalty drama
news.lede: England’s Under-15 World Cup campaign in Azerbaijan witnessed further drama on Friday after they secured a 3-2 victory over Bolivia courtesy of an uncontested late penalty. The South American team’s goalkeeper made no attempt to stop the spot-kick in the dying moments of the fixture, which established the final scoreline. Following the goal, Bolivian players appeared to angrily confront the referee as well as their English counterparts before both squads eventually headed off the pitch. The Football Association has been approached for comment regarding Friday’s fixture, while governing body Fifa will await the report from the match delegate before deciding whether to take any further action.

news.title: India U-15 secure 87th place finish in FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 in Baku
news.lede: Blue Colts scored 30 goals across 10 games The FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival 2026 kicked off in Baku, Azerbaijan, a week ago, and after ten games, India U-15 finally wrapped their campaign in Baku with a 6-4 victory against Cuba to finish 87th among 189 teams from the length and breadth of this planet. India U-15 were drawn in Group K, and until the final matchweek, India were the sole unbeaten team in the group and favourites to top the group and qualify for Tier A. The Blue Colts, led by Bibiano Fernandes, had an impressive campaign and too many moments to cherish in Baku. From trailing 2-0 down against Trinidad and Tobago to clinching a 3-2 comeback win, upsetting African heavyweight Cameroon 2-1 to a four-goal masterclass from Victor Lalawmpuia, the Blue Colts can be proud of their efforts as the team sealed their Baku journey on an exhilarating note against Cuba.
